title: How K changes with temperature
caption: Raising the temperature favours the endothermic direction. For the exothermic Haber process (ΔH = −92 kJ mol⁻¹) K falls as T rises; for the endothermic N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂ (ΔH = +57 kJ mol⁻¹) K rises. Shown as ln(K/K₂₉₈) from the van 't Hoff equation.
alt: ln(K/K at 298 K) against temperature from 298 to 500 K: a falling curve for the exothermic reaction and a rising one for the endothermic reaction.
description: Both start at zero at 298 K.
Exothermic (Haber): ln(K/K₂₉₈) falls to about −15 by 500 K.

checks.name: exothermic: K at 400 K is smaller than at 298 K
endothermic: K at 400 K is larger
